context.significance: The Strait of Hormuz is the world's most critical oil chokepoint, through which roughly 20% of global petroleum trade passes, meaning any sustained closure or militarization of the waterway carries immediate consequences for global energy prices and supply chains. Trump's territorial claim — whether rhetorical or a policy signal — represents an unprecedented assertion by a U.S. president over an internationally recognized international strait, raising fundamental questions about freedom of navigation norms that underpin global maritime law. The expiration of the 60-day MOU without a successor agreement, combined with an active naval blockade and no diplomatic channel, marks a significant escalation point in what is already an active armed conflict with Iran.
outlook: Watch whether the U.S. Navy enforces or extends the naval blockade now that the 60-day MOU has expired.
